name: Meropenem
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Complicated skin and skin structure infections
usual_adult_dose.dose: 500 mg IV every 8 hours (1 g every 8 hours if Pseudomonas aeruginosa)
Infuse over 15 to 30 minutes; 1 g doses may also be given as an IV bolus (5 to 20 mL) over 3 to 5 minutes
26–50: usual dose every 12 hours; 10–25: half dose every 12 hours; below 10: half dose every 24 hours

key_interactions.effect: Valproate levels can fall below the therapeutic range; breakthrough seizures.
key_interactions.action: Generally not recommended; prefer a non-carbapenem; if needed, consider supplemental anticonvulsant.

key_interactions.effect: Competes for tubular secretion; higher meropenem levels.

common: Headache, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, anemia, vomiting, rash (≥2%)

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to product components or other drugs in the same class
monitoring: Seizure activity, especially with CNS disorders or kidney impairment

pk.peak: End of 30-minute infusion: about 23 mcg/mL (500 mg) and 49 mcg/mL (1 g); 5-minute bolus: about 45 mcg/mL (500 mg) and 112 mcg/mL (1 g)
pk.half_life_eskd: About 6.8 hours in ESKD (vs 0.9 hours healthy; Christensson 1992); 7.0 hours off dialysis, 2.9 hours during hemodialysis (Chimata 1993)
pk.metabolism: One microbiologically inactive metabolite (about 28% of dose)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 70% (50% to 75%) unchanged in urine within 12 hours
pk.dialyzability: Yes: readily dialyzable and effectively removed by hemodialysis (label); dialysis clearance about 79 mL/min/1.73 m2 (Christensson 1992).

draft_notes: Batch 3: label is now a 500 mg / 1 g single-dose vial (Civica, ANDA206086) instead of the B. Braun DUPLEX premixed container. Removed the premix-only contraindication (sodium/chloride) and the 'high sodium load' adverse effect; added IV bolus administration and the renal schedule row.
Meningitis is a pediatric-only indication; it is no longer in the adult dose list.
ESKD half-life is from two small 1990s PK studies (n=4 to 5 ESKD patients each), PubMed-verified; label has none.
Platelet monitoring in kidney impairment is our inference from label 5.8 (thrombocytopenia seen in renal impairment, no bleeding); the label sets no schedule.

revision_log.change: Pediatric meningitis row removed from adult doses (already in pediatric dosing).
